Local Extraction Test

A useful article begins with a clear explanation and enough context for a reader to understand the subject without visiting another page.

Readable content should preserve paragraphs, headings, links, code examples, and the relationships between ideas while removing navigation and promotional material.

Local extraction gives the caller a deterministic fallback when a remote reader is unavailable or returns a sparse result. It also makes metadata and quality checks available to the command itself.

The implementation should remain conservative. It should prefer a smaller correct article over a larger result that includes unrelated sidebars, comments, advertisements, or footer text.

Testing uses intentionally noisy pages because real websites contain repeated labels, hidden elements, responsive navigation, partial content selectors, and old table layouts that can confuse a generic parser.

When a first pass removes too much content, a bounded retry can relax one rule at a time. The retry should be accepted only when a measurable quality signal improves and the result still passes safety checks.

Relative links and images should resolve against the final response URL. Unsafe schemes and attributes should be removed before content is returned to callers or rendered by another tool.

Metadata should use deterministic precedence across the document title, standard meta tags, OpenGraph, Twitter cards, canonical URLs, and structured data. Missing fields should remain empty rather than being guessed.

These paragraphs intentionally contain enough words to exercise the normal extraction path while keeping the fixture readable. A real implementation can add more site-specific fixtures when a known platform needs specialized handling.
